what_the_class_is: The rotary multi: a drive, an equaliser and the rotary, then the output level. Each part is the candidate its stand-alone type's stage put first, re-bound to this type's own addresses.

era.when: Mid nineteen-nineties, a custom fixed-point DSP running its effects at 32 kHz with a small control processor beside it.
what_that_implies: A block that several types name is one routine reached with a parameter block, so a combination is its single effects called one after another or side by side, and its own code is the wiring and the level, pan and mix multipliers between them.
A stage switched off is a jump over its routine, so what reaches the next stage is what reached the switched one.
Placing a half of a pair is two multipliers on its output; moving a stereo pair costs two more.
era.would_be_wrong_if: A setting nothing here was fitted on came back with a part answering in a place the arrangement does not put it -- a level byte at nothing leaving the other half on a series reading, or silencing it on a parallel one.

candidates.reading: The drive, then the equaliser, then the rotary, in the order the page prints them.
candidates.predicts: The equaliser's shelves and mid shape what the drive has already made, so they move its harmonics along with the note.

candidates.reading: The equaliser in front of the drive, the rotary last.
candidates.predicts: A boost at the equaliser drives that band harder and changes the harmonic balance; a cut there removes it from what the curve sees.
